wortfallen.lead: Some words look like a word you already know, or like a word from your own language, and mean something completely different. Here are {n} traps, each with a memory trick.
wortfallen.camera.react: A new room, and you take photos with it? Where is the lens?
wortfallen.camera.tip: False friend for English speakers. In Italian, camera is a room, usually the bedroom: camera da letto. The device is la macchina fotografica (or la fotocamera).
wortfallen.parenti.react: Your mum and dad are relatives too, but Italian has a special word for them.
wortfallen.parenti.tip: False friend for English speakers (parents), and for French speakers (parents). I parenti are all your relatives: uncles, cousins, grandparents. Mother and father are i genitori.
wortfallen.libreria.react: Borrowing from a shop? The bookseller will want to see your wallet.
wortfallen.libreria.tip: False friend for English speakers. A library, where you borrow books, is la biblioteca. In una libreria you buy them.
wortfallen.morbido.react: A soft film about death? Cuddly, but not quite.
wortfallen.morbido.tip: False friend for English speakers (morbid). morbido means soft, like a pillow or a cheese. Morbid in the dark sense is morboso or macabro.
wortfallen.educato.react: She is polite, sure. But the two degrees say something else.
wortfallen.educato.tip: False friend for English speakers (educated). educato means polite, with good manners (the noun is l'educazione). Educated, with schooling, is istruito, colto or laureato.
wortfallen.eventualmente.react: Possibly found a flat? Did you find it or not?
wortfallen.eventualmente.tip: False friend for English speakers (eventually). eventualmente means if the case arises, possibly: bring a copy, eventualmente a photocopy. Eventually is alla fine, prima o poi or col tempo. Same trap with the adjective eventuale (possible).
wortfallen.attualmente.react: Currently forty years old? Everyone is, at the moment.
wortfallen.attualmente.tip: False friend for English speakers (actually). attualmente means at the moment: attualmente lavoro a Torino. Actually, in fact is in realtà, davvero or veramente. Same for attuale (current).
wortfallen.firma.react: A signature that makes shoes? Impressive.
wortfallen.firma.tip: False friend for English speakers (firm) and for German speakers (Firma). la firma is a signature. A company is la ditta, l'azienda or la società.
wortfallen.fattoria.react: Cars growing on a farm? Plant a Fiat and see.
wortfallen.fattoria.tip: False friend for English speakers (factory). la fattoria is a farm with animals; a factory is la fabbrica or lo stabilimento.
wortfallen.simpatico.react: Nice is fine, but your boss did more than that: he understood.
wortfallen.simpatico.tip: False friend for English speakers (sympathetic). simpatico means likeable, nice company. For understanding and compassion use comprensivo or solidale. To say you feel sorry: mi dispiace.
wortfallen.pretendere.react: The children demand to sleep? Not what they are doing.
wortfallen.pretendere.tip: False friend for English speakers (to pretend). pretendere means to demand or to expect: pretendo rispetto. To pretend is fingere or far finta di.
wortfallen.sensibile.react: A sensitive decision? Careful, it might cry.
wortfallen.sensibile.tip: False friend for English speakers (sensible). sensibile means sensitive: una pelle sensibile, una persona sensibile. Sensible, reasonable is ragionevole or sensato.
wortfallen.assistere.react: You attended grandma's shopping like a match. Did you at least carry the bags?
wortfallen.assistere.tip: False friend for English speakers (to assist): assistere a means to be present at, to watch (assistere a una lezione, a un incidente). To help is aiutare. assistere without a is to look after a sick person: assistere un malato.
wortfallen.cantina.react: Lunch in the cellar with your colleagues? Cosy, but dark.
wortfallen.cantina.tip: False friend for English speakers (canteen). la cantina is a cellar, or a winery (la cantina sociale). A work or school canteen is la mensa.
wortfallen.conveniente.react: Good value because of the metro stop? Nice, but the price isn't the point.
wortfallen.conveniente.tip: False friend for English speakers (convenient). conveniente is about money: it pays off, it's a good price. Convenient in the sense of practical and handy is comodo or pratico.
wortfallen.ritirare.react: Your uncle withdraws from work like money from a cash machine.
wortfallen.ritirare.tip: False friend for English speakers (to retire). ritirare means to take back or collect: ritirare un pacco, i soldi, il permesso di soggiorno. Retire from work is andare in pensione.
wortfallen.tasca.react: A red leather pocket? Not many trousers have those.
wortfallen.tasca.tip: False friend for German speakers (Tasche). la tasca is the pocket sewn in clothes. A bag you carry is la borsa (also la borsetta, la sacca). Also: la borsa is the stock exchange.
wortfallen.mappa.react: All your papers in a blue map? You'll get lost at the counter.
wortfallen.mappa.tip: False friend for German speakers (die Mappe = folder). la mappa is a map. For papers, use la cartella (also il raccoglitore, la cartellina). A hint for the Questura: bring all your documents in una cartella.
wortfallen.confetti.react: Throwing sugared almonds at people in the street? That hurts.
wortfallen.confetti.tip: False friend for English and German speakers (confetti / Konfetti). i confetti are sugared almonds, given at weddings and baptisms. The paper bits thrown at Carnevale are i coriandoli.
wortfallen.burro.react: A butter in the stable that eats hay? Sounds greasy.
wortfallen.burro.tip: False friend for Spanish speakers: burro = el asno in Spanish, but il burro is butter in Italian. The animal is l'asino or il somaro.
wortfallen.salire.react: Going up with your friends? Is the cinema on the roof?
wortfallen.salire.tip: False friend for Spanish speakers: salir = to go out, but salire is to go up (also: to get on a bus or train: salire sul treno). To go out is uscire.
wortfallen.largo.react: A river a thousand kilometres wide? That's a sea.
wortfallen.largo.tip: False friend for Spanish speakers (largo = long) and for French speakers (large = wide, which is the same as Italian). Italian largo means wide; long is lungo. In music, largo is a slow tempo.
wortfallen.carta.react: You wrote a paper to your grandmother? Hopefully she wasn't graded.
wortfallen.carta.tip: False friend for Spanish speakers (carta = letter) and Portuguese speakers (carta = letter). In Italian la carta is paper, also a card (la carta d'identità, la carta di credito). A letter is la lettera.
wortfallen.guardare.react: Looking at it in a drawer? It's not going anywhere.
wortfallen.guardare.tip: False friend for Spanish speakers (guardar = to keep) and Portuguese speakers (guardar = to keep). Italian guardare is to look. To keep, to store is tenere, conservare or mettere via.
wortfallen.sale.react: A salty shirt? Did you swim in it?
wortfallen.sale.tip: False friend for French speakers: French sale = dirty, Italian il sale = salt (masculine!). Dirty is sporco, and the Italian adjective for salty is salato.
wortfallen.tante.react: Having lunch at 'so many'? Whose house is this?
wortfallen.tante.tip: False friend for French speakers (tante = aunt) and for German speakers (Tante = aunt). Italian tante is many: tante persone. An aunt is la zia.
wortfallen.polvo.react: Grilled dust with potatoes? Not even the dog would eat it.
wortfallen.polvo.tip: False friend for Portuguese speakers: polvo = the octopus in Portuguese, but la polvere is dust in Italian (the animal is il polpo). Also for Spanish speakers: polvo = dust, same as Italian.
wortfallen.squisito.react: Delicious behaviour, but he never says hello? Odd taste.
wortfallen.squisito.tip: False friend for Portuguese speakers: esquisito = strange in Portuguese, but squisito means delicious or refined in Italian. Strange is strano or bizzarro.

verben.mascot: You need these verbs every day.
verben.lead: A mini grammar to look things up: {n} verbs in every tense and mood, all six persons. Whatever doesn't follow the pattern is <mark class="vb-x">highlighted</mark>: that's what you have to learn.
verben.group.hilfsverb.name: essere, avere, stare, andare
verben.group.hilfsverb.what: The four verbs you need from day one. All four are irregular in the present, the passato remoto and the congiuntivo.
verben.group.modal.name: Verb + infinitive
verben.group.modal.what: They say what is possible, wanted, necessary or usual. A second verb follows, in the infinitive.
verben.group.unregelmaessig.name: Irregular verbs
verben.group.unregelmaessig.what: Each has its own forms, shown highlighted, but they fall into groups you can learn together.
verben.group.regelmaessig.name: Regular verbs
verben.group.regelmaessig.what: Take -are, -ere or -ire off the infinitive and add the endings. Most verbs work like this, and new verbs do too.
verben.group.isc.name: -ire verbs with -isc-
verben.group.isc.what: Many -ire verbs add -isc- in io, tu, lui/lei and loro (finisco, finisci, finisce, finiscono), but not in noi and voi (finiamo, finite).
verben.group.spelling.name: Spelling changes
verben.group.spelling.what: The spelling adapts so that the sound stays the same: cerco → cerchi, mangio → mangi.
verben.group.trennbar.name: Reflexive and pronominal verbs
verben.group.trennbar.what: Verb + pronoun (mi, ti, si, ci, vi, si). The pronoun changes with the person: mi alzo alle sette, si alza alle otto.

schreiben.check.a1-formular-anmeldung.0: “Nome” is your first name and “cognome” your surname. Some forms ask for “Cognome e nome” in that order, so read the label before you copy.
schreiben.check.a1-formular-anmeldung.1: The date is day/month/year: 04/03/1996. 03/04/1996 would be 3 April.
schreiben.check.a1-formular-anmeldung.2: “CAP” (the postcode) and “Comune” (the town) go in separate fields, even if they are together in the text.
schreiben.check.a1-formular-anmeldung.3: The address is street, comma, number: “via dell'Olmo, 12”. Keep the apostrophe and the accent marks of the text.
schreiben.check.a1-nachricht-absage.0: All four points are there: in an exam, a missing point costs more than a small grammar mistake.
schreiben.check.a1-nachricht-absage.1: There is a greeting and a sign-off (Ciao Giulia! / Un abbraccio).
schreiben.check.a1-nachricht-absage.2: Accents are part of the spelling: “perché”, “caffè”, “è”. Without them the word is wrong, even if you can read it.
schreiben.check.a1-nachricht-absage.3: The sentences are short. At A1, “Devo lavorare.” is better than a long sentence with a mistake.
schreiben.check.a2-email-nachbarn.0: The requests are questions (“Potrebbe…?”, “Le dispiacerebbe…?”), not orders (“Annaffi le mie piante”, “Deve…”).
schreiben.check.a2-email-nachbarn.1: After “Le dispiacerebbe…?” comes the infinitive: “Le dispiacerebbe ritirare la posta?”.
schreiben.check.a2-email-nachbarn.2: “Lei” all the way through: “le porto”, “il suo aiuto”, “potrebbe”. One “tu” in the middle would stand out.
schreiben.check.a2-email-nachbarn.3: Greeting and sign-off match: “Buongiorno, signora Conti,” → “Cordiali saluti”. “Un abbraccio” is too familiar for a neighbour you hardly know.
schreiben.check.a2-email-school.0: “Ha la febbre” with “avere”: “è la febbre” or “ha febbre” are typical mistakes.
schreiben.check.a2-email-school.1: The teacher can tell at once which child and which class it is about.
schreiben.check.a2-email-school.2: A polite question: “Potrebbe dirmi…?”. Some schools use “tu” with parents; “Lei” is the safe choice in a first message.
schreiben.check.a2-formular-arztpraxis.0: Numbers are spoken, not written: “il venti novembre millenovecentoottantotto” → 20/11/1988. A mobile number is often said digit by digit or in groups: “tre quattro cinque, zero zero zero…” → 345 000 0315 (a placeholder).
schreiben.check.a2-formular-arztpraxis.1: Careful with “Prima visita?”. He answers “No” to a different question (“È già stato in questo studio?”), so here the right answer is “sì”.
schreiben.check.a2-formular-arztpraxis.2: “Perfetto” means the appointment is confirmed, so fill in the doctor, the day and the time. “Alle tre e mezza del pomeriggio” is 15:30.
schreiben.check.a2-padron-form.0: An Italian address runs street, number, then the flat: “via delle Fornaci, 5, interno 3”.
schreiben.check.a2-padron-form.1: “Comune di provenienza” asks where you lived before: Bologna, not Casalbruno and not Tangeri.
schreiben.check.a2-padron-form.2: Copy your codice fiscale exactly, letter by letter. The one here is a made-up placeholder.
schreiben.check.a2-padron-form.3: This is language practice, not official guidance: the real form and the papers to bring vary, so ask at your own Comune (Ufficio Anagrafe).
schreiben.check.b1-email-landlord.0: All four points are there, and the landlady can act on them: what is broken, since when, when someone can come.
schreiben.check.b1-email-landlord.1: The tenses tell the story: “si è rotta lunedì” (one event, passato prossimo) and “non abbiamo” after “da allora” (still true now).
schreiben.check.b1-email-landlord.2: “Lei” throughout, and a comma after the greeting: “Gentile signora Ferrari,”. Unlike in some other languages, Italian does not use a colon there.
schreiben.check.b1-email-landlord.3: “Preferisce che lo chiami io”: “preferire che” takes the congiuntivo.
schreiben.check.b1-email-employer.0: A solution comes with the request: the boss reads “posso scambiare il turno con Matteo” and only has to say yes.
schreiben.check.b1-email-employer.1: “Tu” with your boss is normal in many Italian workplaces. If yours uses “Lei”, keep to it: “Le scrivo per chiederLe un favore”.
schreiben.check.b1-email-employer.2: The tone is a request, not an announcement: “Se per te va bene” softens it.
schreiben.check.b1-email-employer.3: Time off for official appointments depends on your contract and your “contratto collettivo”; this task practises the email, not your rights.
schreiben.check.b2-beschwerde-reiseveran: No angry words: “Mi dispiace comunicarvi che si sono verificati diversi problemi gravi” instead of “è una vergogna”. At B2 the tone is part of the mark: firm, but never rude.
Each problem is set against a promise (“Nel vostro catalogo… In realtà…”). A complaint without that comparison is only an opinion.
There is a clear demand AND a deadline. Without a date, a letter of complaint is not complete.
B2 linking words and forms: “poiché”, “inoltre”, “pertanto”, “senza che” + congiuntivo, “in mancanza di”. “Spettabile Agenzia,” with a comma, then “Distinti saluti”.
schreiben.check.b2-opinion-text.0: The position is clear in the first paragraph, and the last paragraph comes back to it.
schreiben.check.b2-opinion-text.1: Each argument has an example of its own. “Sarebbe più sicuro” alone is a claim; the two streets on the way to school make it real.
schreiben.check.b2-opinion-text.2: The other side gets a fair sentence before the answer: “È vero che…; tuttavia…”.
schreiben.check.b2-opinion-text.3: B2 forms: the conditional for what would happen (“migliorerebbe”, “trarrebbe vantaggio”), “non si tratta di…, ma di…”, “preferisco che” + congiuntivo.
schreiben.check.b1-formular-vhs.0: Every field is filled in. An empty field counts as a mistake, even if the information is in the text.
schreiben.check.b1-formular-vhs.1: Copy names, numbers and dates exactly as they are in the text, with their accents; in Italy the day comes before the month (12 settembre, 12/09).
schreiben.check.b1-formular-vhs.2: Nothing made up: if something is not in the text, leave the field empty or put a dash.
schreiben.check.b1-brief-david.0: Every point in the task is covered. A missing point costs more than three grammar mistakes.
schreiben.check.b1-brief-david.1: Greeting and sign-off suit each other and the person: an office gets “Gentile Ufficio Anagrafe, … Cordiali saluti”, a friend “Ciao …, … Un abbraccio”.
schreiben.check.b1-brief-david.2: The sentences are linked (perciò, perché, ma, inoltre, anche se), not just one after the other.
schreiben.check.b1-fehlerjagd.0: Read first, then compare: discuss the text only once you have marked every mistake you can find.
schreiben.check.b1-fehlerjagd.1: The text has about 20 mistakes. Look at: gender and agreement (“il problema”, “molto sporche”), articles before a vowel (“l'ingresso”), regular endings added to irregular participles (“messo”), essere or avere in the passato prossimo, the congiuntivo after “vorrei che”, accents (“perché”, “è”), double consonants, capital letters in months, a pleonastic pronoun (“non gli importa”), and a closing line translated word for word from English.
schreiben.check.b1-fehlerjagd.2: Write down the mistakes you make yourself, too. That is the point of the task.

telcSb.t.5bbc7d51: Grammar and vocabulary inside a running text, not in single sentences: the kind of skill the language-structure tasks of the higher-level papers ask for. Here once as matching from a word box and once as multiple choice.
telcSb.t.1f789aa1: Which word from the box fits which gap? Each word fits only once; two words are left over.
telcSb.t.8149bd55: Which word fits? For each gap, click one of the three options.
telcSb.t.96e0ef92: Task 1 — a word box with ten words or phrases but only eight gaps. Two are left over; each fits only once.
telcSb.t.9da06361: Task 2 — ten gaps, three options for each. Often it is not grammar alone that decides, but which word goes with the words around it.
telcSb.t.4239832e: Both tasks test connectors, prepositions, verb forms (indicative or subjunctive) and fixed expressions, always in context.
telcSb.t.7807a6e0: Strategy: read the whole text once first, then fill the gaps you are sure of and the hard ones last. In Task 1 elimination helps: every word you place is gone for the remaining gaps. Always read the words before and after the gap.

delesiele.title: CILS, CELI, PLIDA or CERT.IT?
delesiele.lead: These four certificates of Italian as a foreign language are the ones offices and universities most often ask for. What decides between them is what you need the result for. For citizenship the level is usually B1, for the long-term EU residence permit usually A2. Which certificates the office accepts is for the office to say, so ask first.
delesiele.purpose.title: What do you need it for?
delesiele.purpose.note: General orientation, not legal advice. Rules change (the citizenship rules changed in 2025), so before you pay for an exam, check with the office that will read your result: the Ministero dell'Interno portal, your Prefettura or Questura, or your Comune.
delesiele.compare.title: The four certificates side by side
delesiele.compare.note: Written in November 2026 and still to be checked against the official pages. Formats, results, validity and prices differ by certificate, level and country and change over time, so we don't list them here. Check the official page of the certificate you plan to take.
delesiele.tips.title: If you still can't decide
delesiele.tips.1: You don't know your level yet: try a practice test first and register only for a level you can reach. A certificate at the wrong level can end in a fail.
delesiele.tips.2: You need the result for an office: ask which certificates it accepts, at which level and how old they may be, before you book.
delesiele.tips.3: You need a result soon: compare the next session dates on the official pages. They differ by certificate and by centre.
delesiele.tips.4: You want the certificate to last: how long it is valid differs by certificate and by office, so check this before you choose.
delesiele.tips.5: You mostly hear one regional Italian: listen to the official sample recordings and practise understanding other accents too.

testdaf.day.1: Each skill has its own part: listening, reading, writing and speaking (ascoltare, leggere, scrivere, parlare).
testdaf.day.2: You register for one level. Choose the level you need, not the highest you might reach.
testdaf.day.3: Speaking is a conversation at the exam centre. Be ready to talk about yourself, describe a situation and give your opinion.
testdaf.day.4: In the written parts, accents and double consonants count: perché, città, anno, sono.
testdaf.day.5: Dates, prices and how long results take are set by the exam centres. Ask yours.

delesiele.p.nationality.answer: Usually B1, from a recognised certifying body
delesiele.p.nationality.text: For citizenship by residence or by marriage, the usual language proof is a certificate at B1 or higher. CILS, CELI, PLIDA and CERT.IT are the certifying bodies usually named for this. The rules changed in 2025 and some applicants are exempt, for example with a school or university diploma from Italy, so check your own case on the Ministero dell'Interno citizenship portal or with your Prefettura.
delesiele.p.university.title: University and study
delesiele.p.university.text: Universities that teach in Italian usually want a certificate at B2 or higher, but each university and each degree sets its own rule. Some name certain certificates, some run their own test. Get the rule in writing from the admissions office (segreteria studenti) and ask how old your certificate may be.
delesiele.p.work.title: Work
delesiele.p.work.text: Private employers often care more about your level than about which certificate it came from. Public jobs and regulated professions can have fixed rules: check the call for applications (bando) or the professional body. If you have a choice, compare the next session dates, because they differ by certificate and by centre.
delesiele.p.visa.title: Long-term EU residence permit
delesiele.p.visa.text: For the permesso di soggiorno UE per soggiornanti di lungo periodo, you usually have to show Italian at A2. A certificate at A2 or higher from a recognised body is normally accepted instead of the Italian test given by the Prefettura. Ask your Questura or Prefettura which certificates it takes and whether you are exempt. This page is general orientation, not legal advice.
delesiele.p.self.title: For yourself
delesiele.p.self.text: If you want a goal to work towards, any of the four gives you a level to aim for and a certificate if you reach it. Which one fits depends on how and when you want to sit the exam, so compare the formats on the official pages.

nat.title: Italian citizenship and the long-term permit: the language proof
nat.lead: Most adults who apply for Italian citizenship by residence or marriage must show Italian at B1, and the long-term EU residence permit asks for A2. On this page: who needs what, who may be exempt, what changed in 2025 and the order of the steps.
nat.legal: General orientation, not legal advice. The rules on citizenship and residence permits change (the citizenship rules changed in 2025), and each office applies them in its own way. For your own case, check the Interior Ministry's pages, your Prefettura or Questura, or ask an immigration lawyer or an advice organisation such as a patronato.
nat.short.title: The short version
nat.short.1: Citizenship by residence needs a number of years of legal residence in Italy. How many depends on your situation and nationality.
nat.short.2: For citizenship by residence or marriage you usually need an Italian language certificate at B1 or higher from CILS, CELI, PLIDA or CERT.IT, unless you are exempt.
nat.short.3: The long-term EU residence permit (permesso di soggiorno UE per soggiornanti di lungo periodo) asks for Italian at A2: a test at the Prefettura, or a certificate at A2 or higher.
nat.short.4: You apply for citizenship online to the Interior Ministry, and the Prefettura handles the file. Check the current steps, documents and fees before you start.
nat.other: This page only covers the language proof. Citizenship by descent (iure sanguinis) and other routes have their own rules.

dgt.orient.title: The driving licence in Italy: a short orientation
dgt.orient.legal: General orientation, not legal advice. Rules and exam details change. Check the official site of the Ministry of Infrastructure and Transport (Ministero delle Infrastrutture e dei Trasporti) or your local Motorizzazione before you rely on anything here.
dgt.orient.1: For the Italian licence B, you usually pass a theory exam (esame di teoria) and a practical test (prova pratica). Most people go to a driving school (autoscuola). Whether you can prepare without one is something to check with the Motorizzazione.
dgt.orient.2: You also need a medical certificate. Ask your driving school or the Motorizzazione who can issue it.
dgt.orient.3: The format of the theory test, the number of questions and the pass mark change from time to time. Check the current rules with your driving school or the Motorizzazione.
dgt.orient.4: The theory test may be available in some other languages besides Italian. Which ones, and how to ask for it, is something to verify when you apply. Even then, signs, instructions and papers will be in Italian.
dgt.orient.5: If you already hold a licence from another country, you may be able to convert it (conversione della patente) instead of taking the exams. This depends on the country that issued it, so check your case with the Motorizzazione first. A sworn translation (traduzione giurata) may be asked for.

ap.ex.afem: “{word}” starts with a vowel, so the article is l' whatever the gender: l'{word}. This one is {ending}; the plural shows it.
ap.ex.ending: “{word}” ends in {ending}, and nouns with that ending are usually {kind}: {article} {word}.
ap.ex.exception: “{word}” ends in {ending}, which usually means “{expected}”, but this one takes “{article}”: {article} {word}. An exception to learn.
ap.ex.none: This ending does not tell you the gender. Learn the noun together with its article: {article} {word}.
ap.ex.afem.leicht: This word starts with a vowel. So you say “l'”: l'{word}.

ap.ex.sound.leicht: This masculine word starts with {ending}. So you say “lo”: lo {word}.
ap.ex.ending.leicht: The word ends in {ending}. So you say “{article}”: {article} {word}.
ap.ex.exception.leicht: This word does not follow the rule. You say “{article} {word}”.
ap.ex.none.leicht: There is no rule here. Learn the word with its article: {article} {word}.

akd.note.indefinite: You hear the definite article: “{article}”, not “{said}”.
akd.note.notArticle: “{said}” is not an article. It is “{article}”.

ap.hint.title.text: Learning gender through rules only takes you so far, because many rules have exceptions (la mano, il problema, la radio). What works best is learning every noun together with its article (il libro, lo zaino, la casa, l'acqua), for example in the vocabulary trainer, and then meeting the words in everyday life. Treat the rules as help with a new word. The reliable ones: -zione, -sione, -tà, -tù → feminine (la stazione, la città); -ore → masculine (il dottore, il colore).
ap.regel.intro: Every Italian noun is masculine or feminine. The article shows the gender, and it also depends on the first sound of the noun: il, lo or l' for masculine, la or l' for feminine. The ending is often a clue: -o is usually masculine, -a usually feminine, -e can be either. These patterns help when you meet a new word, but they have exceptions, so learn each noun with its article.
ap.regel.people: With people the article follows the person: il ragazzo / la ragazza, l'amico / l'amica, lo studente / la studentessa, il collega / la collega. For many words there is no pattern at all, and the article simply has to be learned with the word.
ap.ex.greek: “{word}” is one of the words in -ma that come from Greek. They are masculine, unlike la mamma or la forma: il {word}.
ap.ex.greek.leicht: This word ends in -ma, but you say “il”: il {word}.

certit.lead: The Italian certificate of the Università degli Studi Roma Tre, with one exam per level. Here you can practise in its style at A2.
certit.who.title: Who is the CERT.IT for?
certit.who.text: The CERT.IT (Certificazione dell'Italiano come lingua straniera) is issued by the Università degli Studi Roma Tre, one of the four certifying bodies recognised by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. People use it for study, for work and, at the level required, as the language proof for citizenship or the long-term residence permit. Check what your office or university asks for before you book.
certit.diff.title: How this differs from the real exam
certit.diff.text: Our A2 set follows the general shape of an A2 exam, but every text and task is our own, and our timings and marks are a guide, not the official ones. The Università Roma Tre publishes the current format and sample papers; we do not copy them. Check the details on certit.it before you book. We aren't connected with the Università Roma Tre.

nat.two.title: Two different proofs
nat.two.b1.title: B1 for citizenship
nat.two.b1.text: For citizenship by residence (per residenza) or by marriage (per matrimonio), the language proof is usually a certificate at B1 or higher from a recognised body: CILS, CELI, PLIDA or CERT.IT. Since 2018 it is a condition of the application. To verify: the exact wording of the rule and which certificates the Ministry accepts today.
nat.two.a2.title: A2 for the long-term EU permit
nat.two.a2.text: The long-term EU residence permit (permesso di soggiorno UE per soggiornanti di lungo periodo) asks for Italian at A2. You can show it with a test at the Prefettura or with a certificate at A2 or higher. To verify: how the test is booked and run in your province, and the other conditions (years of legal residence, income, housing).
nat.two.note: A B1 certificate also covers A2, so one B1 certificate can serve both purposes. Levels follow the CEFR scale.
nat.exempt.title: Who may be exempt (to verify)
nat.exempt.intro: Exemptions exist, but they are narrow and the lists change. Ask the office that handles your file before you decide not to sit an exam. Categories that are often named:
nat.exempt.1: People who hold a diploma or degree from an Italian school or university (the study must be recognised in Italy).
nat.exempt.2: People who already hold a certificate at the right level from a recognised body, or a certificate from a CPIA (public adult education centre) at A2.
nat.exempt.3: People who signed the integration agreement (Accordo di integrazione) and meet its conditions.
nat.exempt.4: People with a serious health problem or a disability that makes the test impossible, with medical documents.
nat.exempt.5: Some categories of permit holders, for example under certain protection statuses. The details differ from case to case.
nat.changes.title: What changed in 2025 (to verify)
nat.changes.1: In spring 2025 the rules on citizenship by descent (iure sanguinis) were tightened by decree-law. This does not change the language proof for residence or marriage, but you will read about it in the news.
nat.changes.2: In June 2025 a referendum asked whether the residence period for citizenship should fall from 10 to 5 years. It did not reach the turnout needed, so the 10-year rule for most non-EU citizens stays.
nat.changes.3: Fees, the online forms and the documents asked for were also updated. Our summary may be out of date by the time you read it.
nat.changes.note: Never plan only on a summary like this one: read the Interior Ministry's current page or ask a patronato.
nat.steps.title: The steps, in order (general orientation, to verify)
nat.step.1.title: 1. Work out your route and your years
nat.step.1.text: Residence, marriage or another route. For residence, count the years of legal residence. Many non-EU citizens need ten; the period is shorter for some groups (for example refugees and EU citizens). Keep your permit valid while you prepare.
nat.step.2.title: 2. Check whether you are exempt
nat.step.2.text: Look at the exemption categories above and ask the office if you are unsure. If you are not exempt, you need the language proof.
nat.step.3.title: 3. Prepare and sit the language exam
nat.step.3.text: Choose CILS, CELI, PLIDA or CERT.IT at B1 (A2 for the long-term permit). Practise with the mocks below, then book at a recognised centre. Check how long a certificate stays valid for your application.
nat.step.4.title: 4. Collect your documents
nat.step.4.text: Typical items: a valid passport, your birth certificate (translated and legalised), a criminal record certificate from your country of origin, your residence certificate and proof of income for the last years. The list depends on your route.
nat.step.5.title: 5. Pay the fee and apply online
nat.step.5.text: You apply on the Interior Ministry's portal and pay a fee. Check the current amount and form before you pay.
nat.step.6.title: 6. Wait for the decision
nat.step.6.text: The Prefettura handles your file. Official waiting times are long and, in practice, often longer than the legal limit.
nat.step.7.title: 7. Take the oath
nat.step.7.text: If the decision is positive, you take an oath of loyalty to the Republic before the registrar of your Comune within a deadline. Only then are you an Italian citizen.
nat.step.a2.title: Long-term permit: the short order
nat.step.a2.text: Check your conditions (years of legal residence, income, housing), get proof of A2 or register for the test at the Prefettura, then apply with the Poste kit and wait for the appointment at the Questura.
